item.title: Bruce Thornton's “Clutchness” Key vs. USC, and Ohio State Needs More of the Same While Vying for NCAA Tournament
item.description: Few Buckeyes have ever deserved an NCAA Tournament bid more than Bruce Thornton. The first four-time team captain in Ohio State history is on track to break the school record of 2,096 career points, set by Dennis Hopson, before his tenure concludes at the end of this season. In his latest game, he passed Kelvin Ransey for fifth all-time, now up to 1,950 points. Such records are only possible due to Thornton’s exemplary loyalty in an era often bereft of it. item.title: Penn State Dominates Ohio State, 36-5, In Battle of Nation’s Top Two Teams
item.description: Ohio State has been one of the two best teams in college wrestling all season, but Penn State proved it’s still the king of the sport on Friday night. After the first 17-0 start in program history, Ohio State suffered its first loss of the year in blowout fashion against the top-ranked and also-unbeaten Nittany Lions, falling 36-5 at Penn State's Bryce Jordan Center. item.title: As Big Ten Continues Push for 24-Team Playoff, Ross Bjork Believes CFP Expansion is “Good for the Game”
item.description: Another round of College Football Playoff expansion probably wouldn’t increase Ohio State’s likelihood of winning national championships, but Ohio State athletic director Ross Bjork still believes the CFP should expand again. From an on-field standpoint, the CFP is already as big as it needs to be for Ohio State. item.title: Ohio State Falters Down the Stretch Against No. 15 Virginia Despite 28-Point Outing From Bruce Thornton
item.description: Bruce Thornton delivered Ohio State to the doorstep of a massive win for its NCAA Tournament résumé, but the Buckeyes couldn't close. Ohio State's offense flatlined in the final 10 minutes of play, scoring seven points in the game’s final quadrant as the Buckeyes (16-9, 8-6 Big Ten) fell to No. 15 Virginia (22-3, 10-2 ACC), 70-66.
